evidence.intree_statement: Class QuiverHomomorphism (G : Quiver) (G' : Quiver) := { fnodes : @nodes G -> @nodes G'; fedgemap : forall x y : @nodes G, edges x y -> edges (fnodes x) (fnodes y); fedgemap_respects : ... Proper (respectful equiv equiv) (@fedgemap x y) }
Program Definition QuiverOfCat (C : Category) : Quiver := {| nodes := obj; edges := hom |}
Definition InducedFunctor {C : Category} (F : QuiverHomomorphism G (QuiverOfCat C)) : @Functor (FreeOnQuiver) C

statement_record.book: A diagram of shape G in a category B is defined to be a graph morphism D : G -> UB into the underlying graph of B.
statement_record.intree: The type QuiverHomomorphism G (QuiverOfCat C) — a node map plus an endpoint-indexed edge map respecting the edge setoids, into the underlying quiver of C — is exactly a graph morphism into UB, and it is the input type of the free-category correspondence (InducedFunctor / UniversalArrowQuiverCat).
statement_record.strength_comparison: same — in-tree quivers carry setoid-valued edge sets (a mild generalization subsuming the book's set-edged graphs via Build_Quiver_Standard_Eq); the library never attaches the word 'diagram' to this type (its limit machinery takes functors as diagrams), but the mathematical notion the book defines is this type, used in precisely the book's role.

evidence.intree_statement: Definition Forgetful : @Functor StrictCat QuiverCategory (via QuiverOfCat and QuiverHomomorphismOfFunctor)

Definition UniversalArrowQuiverCat : @UniversalArrow QuiverCategory StrictCat G Forgetful — FreeOnQuiver G with unit UnitQuiverCatAdjunction is a universal arrow; every QuiverHomomorphism G (QuiverOfCat C) factors uniquely through it as InducedFunctor
Definition FreeCatFunctor : @Functor QuiverCategory StrictCat := (LeftAdjointFunctorFromUniversalArrows Forgetful (fun _ => @UniversalArrowQuiverCat _))
Definition FreeForgetfulAdjunction : Adjunction FreeCatFunctor Forgetful := AdjunctionFromUniversalArrows _ _

statement_record.book: Diagrams D : G -> UB correspond exactly to functors D' : C_G -> B (via D' = UD' o P), giving a bijection Cat(C_G, B) iso Grph(G, UB) natural in G and B; i.e. the free-category functor C : Grph -> Cat is left adjoint to the forgetful U : Cat -> Grph.
statement_record.intree: FreeForgetfulAdjunction : Adjunction FreeCatFunctor Forgetful, with Forgetful : StrictCat ⟶ QuiverCategory and FreeCatFunctor : QuiverCategory ⟶ StrictCat, assembled from per-object universal arrows (UniversalArrowQuiverCat) exactly as the book assembles the adjunction from Theorem 1.
statement_record.strength_comparison: same — the full adjunction (hence the natural hom-set bijection (6)) is proven; it lives over StrictCat rather than the library's weak Cat, which matches Mac Lane's Cat (functors compared strictly), and Test/Issue138.v plus the Free.v header record that the weak Cat provably cannot carry it (the underlying quiver is not invariant under natural isomorphism). Edge sets are setoids, a mild generalization.

evidence.intree_statement: Definition Quotient (C : Category) (R : HomRel C) `{@HomCongruence C R} : Category := {| obj := @obj C; hom := @hom C; homset := fun x y => {| equiv := R x y; ... |}; id := @id C; compose := @compose C; ... |} — same objects and morphisms, hom-equivalence coarsened from ≈ to R
Definition QuotientProj : C ⟶ Quotient C R — identity on objects and on morphisms; only the equivalence coarsens (so f R f' gives Qf ≈ Qf' definitionally)
Definition QuotientLift : Quotient C R ⟶ D, for F : C ⟶ D with HF : forall x y (f g : x ~> y), R x y f g -> fmap[F] f ≈ fmap[F] g
Lemma QuotientLift_proj : fmap[QuotientLift] (fmap[QuotientProj] f) = fmap[F] f (Proof. reflexivity. Qed.)

Lemma QuotientLift_unique (G : Quotient C R ⟶ D) (Hobj : forall x, fobj[G] x = fobj[F] x) (HG : ... hom_cast (Hobj x) (Hobj y) (fmap[G] (fmap[QuotientProj] f)) ≈ fmap[F] f) : forall x y f, hom_cast (Hobj x) (Hobj y) (fmap[G] f) ≈ fmap[QuotientLift] f

statement_record.book: For ANY family R of binary relations on the hom-sets of C there exist a category C/R and a functor Q : C -> C/R, bijective on objects, with (i) f R f' implies Qf = Qf', and (ii) any H : C -> D merging R-related arrows factors uniquely as H = H' o Q. Proof: pass to the least congruence containing R and quotient each hom-set.
statement_record.intree: For R already a HomCongruence: Quotient C R with QuotientProj (identity on objects, so bijective on objects), (i) holds definitionally (the quotient's ≈ IS R), and (ii) is QuotientLift + QuotientLift_proj (definitional factorization) + QuotientLift_unique (uniqueness up to hom_cast along object equalities).
statement_record.strength_comparison: intree-weaker: the hypothesis is stronger — R must already be a congruence (HomCongruence), whereas the book takes an arbitrary relation family and completes it to the least congruence; for a given congruence the conclusion is the same (with Qf = Qf' faithfully rendered as the coarsened setoid ≈, and the projection identity-on-objects, stronger than 'bijective on objects').

gap: The least-congruence completion is missing in general: no operator taking an arbitrary HomRel to the smallest HomCongruence containing it (with the induced factorization through it). Congruence-generated closures exist only as bespoke inductives for specific term categories (TermEqW in Construction/PROP/Presentation.v:136, and its coloured analogue), not for an arbitrary category C.

evidence.intree_statement: Class HomCongruence {C : Category} (R : HomRel C) : Type := { cong_incl : f ≈ g -> R x y f g; cong_sym : R x y f g -> R x y g f; cong_trans : R x y f g -> R x y g h -> R x y f h; cong_comp : R y z f f' -> R x y g g' -> R x z (f ∘ g) (f' ∘ g') }
Lemma cong_refl : R x y f f (from cong_incl and reflexivity of ≈)
Lemma Quotient_equivalence : Equivalence (R x y) — each hom-relation of a congruence is an equivalence
Definition Quotient (C : Category) (R : HomRel C) `{@HomCongruence C R} : Category — same objects, hom-setoids coarsened to R, composition induced from C

statement_record.book: A congruence R on C: (i) each R_{a,b} is an equivalence relation on C(a,b); (ii) if f R_{a,b} f' then (h f g) R (h f' g) for all composable g, h. Every family of relations is contained in a least congruence R'; C/R has the quotient hom-sets C(a,b)/R' with induced composition, and any functor whose kernel contains R also contains R'.
statement_record.intree: HomCongruence: per-hom equivalence (cong_sym, cong_trans, reflexivity via cong_incl from ≈) closed under composition on both sides simultaneously (cong_comp); Quotient C R realizes C/R by coarsening the hom-setoids (the setoid-library form of quotient hom-sets).
statement_record.strength_comparison: same for the congruence notion — cong_comp's simultaneous two-sided form and Mac Lane's fixed-flank form (h f g) R (h f' g) are interderivable given reflexivity (cong_refl); cong_incl (contains ≈) is the faithful setoid strengthening of the book's reflexivity. The least-congruence half of the item has no counterpart.

gap: The 'least congruence' construction is absent in general: no closure operator from an arbitrary HomRel to the smallest containing HomCongruence, and no lemma that a functor merging R-related arrows also merges R'-related ones. That pattern appears only as concrete inductively-generated congruences on syntactic term categories (TermEqW, Construction/PROP/Presentation.v:136-161, described as 'the smallest congruence on Term Σ containing ...').

Definition PresentedCat : Category := @Quotient (FreeCat Σ) (fun m n : nat => @TermEqW m n) TermEqW_Congruence — free-on-generators quotiented by congruence-generated-by-equations, the Mac Lane II.8 recipe run for PROPs (with the universal property in Construction/PROP/Presentation/Universal.v)

'The textbook home of this construction is Mac Lane's Chapter II: §II.7 ... and §II.8 [Quotient Categories] immediately quotients it, with Proposition 8.1 producing the category generated by a graph subject to relations among its paths ... In this library the quotient half is Construction/Quotient.v, and Construction/PROP/Presentation.v runs the same recipe one level down for presented PROPs.'

statement_record.book: When C is the free category on a graph G, the quotient C/R is called the category with generators G and relations R (example: the ordinal 3 presented by three objects, arrows f, g, h and the single relation h = g o f; the one-object case recovers presented monoids).
statement_record.intree: Both halves exist generically (FreeOnQuiver; Quotient by a HomCongruence), and the assembled 'free quotiented by congruence generated by equations' pattern is fully realized one level up for PROPs (PresentedCat := Quotient (FreeCat Σ) TermEqW, with projection functor and universal property) and for coloured PROPs — but never for a bare quiver.
statement_record.strength_comparison: intree-weaker: the general definition 'category with generators G and relations R' over an arbitrary quiver is not assembled — Quotient is never applied to FreeOnQuiver, and there is no generic congruence-generated-by-path-equations closure over a free path category; the recipe is instantiated only at the (symmetric monoidal) PROP level, whose objects are fixed to nat.
